config.title: Type React props for reusable button

intro.title: Type React props for reusable button
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Button component in React with TypeScript. You will learn how to define and use TypeScript interfaces to type the component's props, ensuring it accepts specific data like labels and click handlers. The core concept is using TypeScript's static typing to make your React components more predictable and easier to debug. You'll work with React functional components, TypeScript interfaces, and event handlers to create a button that can be customized across your application.
intro.usecase: Typing React props for reusable buttons is a fundamental pattern in building scalable design systems and component libraries, such as those used in enterprise dashboards, e-commerce platforms, and admin panels. For example, a dashboard might use a typed Button component with props for variants (primary, secondary), sizes, and disabled states across filter controls, data export actions, and modal triggers. This ensures consistency, prevents runtime errors, and simplifies maintenance when teams need to update button behavior or appearance globally. As a developer, you'll apply this daily to create reliable, self-documenting UI components that accelerate feature development and reduce bugs in production.

objectives: Construct a TypeScript interface to define button props
Apply the interface to a React functional component
Implement default values for optional button props
Configure a reusable button component with typed props
Initialize and render the button with different prop values
Manipulate button behavior through typed event handlers
Integrate the typed button component into a parent component

steps.title: Import React and TypeScript types
steps.instruction: Import React and the FC (FunctionComponent) type from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and FC from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a module
import { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React and FC available for creating typed functional components.
successCriteria: React and FC are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and FC from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import both React and FC from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the Button component shell
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Button using the FC type from React. Return null for now.
steps.hint: Use either function Button() {} or const Button: FC = () => {} syntax. Make sure to import FC if you haven't already.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and FC from 'react'

// Create the Button component shell here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Button component function is defined with the FC type and returns null.
successCriteria: Button component is created as a function using FC type and returns null
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created a component named Button that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a functional component called Button that returns null.

steps.title: Define the ButtonProps interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named ButtonProps above the Button component. Include a required 'label' property of type string and an optional 'onClick' property of type () => void.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions inside curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a ButtonProps interface with typed properties that will be used for the Button component's props.
successCriteria: ButtonProps interface is defined with label: string and onClick?: () => void properties
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've included both the required 'label' property and optional 'onClick' property with correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ButtonProps interface isn't properly defined. Remember to use the 'interface' keyword and include the required properties with their types.

steps.title: Add label prop to ButtonProps
steps.instruction: Add a required 'label' property of type string to the ButtonProps interface.
steps.hint: Inside the ButtonProps interface, add a property named 'label' with type 'string'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ButtonProps interface now has a required 'label' property of type string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a 'label' property with type 'string' to the ButtonProps interface.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ButtonProps interface still needs a 'label' property of type string. Check the interface definition.

steps.title: Add onClick prop to ButtonProps
steps.instruction: Add an optional 'onClick' property to the ButtonProps interface with the type '() => void'.
steps.hint: In TypeScript, you can define a function type for a prop. Use a question mark to make it optional.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ButtonProps interface now includes an optional onClick property typed as a function that returns nothing.
successCriteria: ButtonProps interface has an optional onClick property with type '() => void'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an onClick property, but check the type or optional modifier. It should be optional (with '?') and have type '() => void'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onClick prop is missing or incorrect. Add 'onClick?: () => void' to the ButtonProps interface.

steps.title: Add disabled prop to ButtonProps
steps.instruction: Add an optional 'disabled' property of type boolean to the ButtonProps interface.
steps.hint: In TypeScript, you can make a property optional by adding a '?' after its name. The type should be 'boolean'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ButtonProps interface now includes an optional disabled property of type boolean.
successCriteria: ButtonProps has an optional 'disabled' property with type 'boolean'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the disabled property is optional (using '?') and has the correct type 'boolean'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ButtonProps interface should have an optional 'disabled' property of type boolean. Check the syntax for optional properties in TypeScript interfaces.

steps.title: Apply ButtonProps to the component
steps.instruction: Pass the ButtonProps interface as the generic type to FC in the Button component definition.
steps.hint: Add <ButtonProps> after FC to type the component's props.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Button component is now typed with ButtonProps, enabling type checking for its props.
successCriteria: ButtonProps is passed as the generic type to FC in the Button component definition.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you pass ButtonProps as the generic type to FC in the Button component definition.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component is not yet typed with ButtonProps. Pass ButtonProps as the generic type to FC.

steps.title: Destructure props in the component
steps.instruction: Inside the Button component, destructure the label, onClick, and disabled properties from the props parameter.
steps.hint: Use object destructuring syntax in the function parameters to extract the three props defined in your ButtonProps interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Button component will have access to the individual props through destructuring, making them available for use in the component body.
successCriteria: The Button component parameters include destructured label, onClick, and disabled properties from the props object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're destructuring all three props: label, onClick, and disabled from the props parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The props haven't been destructured correctly. Check that you're extracting label, onClick, and disabled from the props parameter.

steps.title: Create the button JSX structure
steps.instruction: Return a button element with the label as its children.
steps.hint: Inside the component's return statement, replace 'null' with a button element. Use the destructured label prop as the button's content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Button component returns a button element with the label prop as its content.
successCriteria: Button component returns a button element
Button element uses the label prop as children
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a button element with the label prop as its children.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element is missing or not correctly using the label prop. Check the return statement.

steps.title: Wire props to button attributes
steps.instruction: In the button JSX element, add the onClick and disabled attributes using the destructured props.
steps.hint: Set onClick to the onClick prop and disabled to the disabled prop.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring props to attributes
<button onClick={handleClick} disabled={isDisabled}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button element should have onClick and disabled attributes connected to the component props.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some attributes, but make sure both onClick and disabled are connected to the destructured props.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button attributes aren't properly connected. Check that you're using the destructured onClick and disabled props.
